indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: Demonstrate an understanding of probability by identifying all possible outcomes of a probability experiment, determining the theoretical and experimental probability of outcomes in a probability experiment
indicator.objective: Predict the probability of a given outcome occurring for a given probability experiment by using theoretical probability

skills.description: Predict the likely result of an experiment using theoretical probability.
Predict from a spinner with unequal sectors.

misconceptions: Expecting exact results from few trials

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed 100 times. About how many times would you expect to get a Head?
questions.misconception: Thinking it must be exactly 50 every time.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled 60 times. About how many times would you expect to roll a 3?
A spinner has 4 equal sectors: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow. If spun 40 times, about how many times would you expect Red?
A fair coin is tossed 20 times. About how many Tails would you expect?
questions.misconception: Thinking it must be more than 10.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled 30 times. About how many times would you expect an even number?
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. If a ball is picked 50 times with replacement, about how many red balls would you expect?
questions.misconception: Using only the number of red balls (4).

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled 120 times. About how many times would you expect a number greater than 4?
A fair coin is tossed 200 times. About how many times would you expect to get a Head?
questions.misconception: Thinking it must be exactly 100 every time.

questions.stem: A coin is tossed 10 times and 7 Heads are recorded. What is the experimental probability of Head?
hints: Experimental probability = number of Heads / total tosses.

questions.stem: A fair coin has theoretical probability of Head = 1/2. In 20 tosses, 8 Heads are recorded. How does the experimental probability compare with the theoretical?
questions.misconception: Thinking any result close to half is equal.

questions.stem: A fair six-sided die is rolled 60 times. The number 6 appears 12 times. What is the experimental probability of rolling a 6?
A fair coin is tossed 100 times. Theoretical P(Head) = 1/2. If 45 Heads are recorded, what is the experimental probability and how does it compare?
questions.misconception: Thinking 45/100 is equal to 1/2 because 45 is close to 50.

questions.stem: A spinner with 4 equal sectors is spun 80 times. The theoretical probability of Red is 1/4. If Red appears 30 times, what is the experimental probability?
A fair die is rolled 600 times. Theoretical P(6) = 1/6. If 80 sixes are recorded, what is the experimental probability and how does it compare?
A spinner has 5 equal sectors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Which outcome is most likely?
hints: The sectors are equal in size.
questions.explanation: All outcomes have the same probability (1/5).
questions.misconception: Thinking larger numbers are more likely.

questions.stem: A spinner has 3 sectors: Red (half the spinner), Blue (quarter), Green (quarter). Which colour is most likely?
hints: Probability is proportional to sector size.
questions.explanation: Red has the largest sector, so it is most likely.
questions.misconception: Thinking all colours are equally likely.

questions.stem: A spinner has 8 equal sectors: 5 are Red and 3 are Blue. What is the probability of landing on Red?
questions.misconception: Using the number of blue sectors.

questions.stem: A spinner has sectors: Red (1/2), Blue (1/4), Green (1/4). If spun 80 times, about how many times would you expect Blue?
A spinner has 10 equal sectors: 6 are Red and 4 are Blue. If spun 50 times, about how many times would you expect Blue?
questions.misconception: Using the number of red sectors (6/10) to predict blue.
